findings_deductions_and_limits.review:
All three actual PDF hashes and page counts match the official assignment; exact values, URLs, boundaries and per-page image hashes are in `source-map.json`. Original cached presentation p19 is zero bytes (SHA-256 e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855) and fails image identification. It remains untouched. The supplied full recovery `/workspace/scratch/ac36b9c5ff31/prof-readability/cache-recovery-20261008/D122-page-019.png` was verified, decoded (1650×1275), and personally opened. Its SHA-256 is `a811940cec9095b0fbd3883e086ee2880ba3d999ddc59d84e4f3c8bd3cff32b3`. An identical copy is `recovered-presentation-p019.png` in this packet; `image-recovery-evidence.json` records both the observed failure and recovery. No cause or time of the failure was established. The recovery closes this review's visual access gap, not the old artifact's state.

Extracted presentation text has disrupted reading order because of the rotated/native PDF layout; the individual full slide images were the controlling visual reading for formulas, arrows, graphs, table entries and captions. PRS p2 contains visible square glyph artifacts after symbols; the relation remains clear and is independently displayed in presentation pp6/10. Nothing consequential is left unread because of those squares.

**Pages 1–10:** Outline and section breaks were read. The capacitor paradox on p4 must compare two surfaces sharing one oriented boundary; the schematic is not a quantitative construction of magnetic field everywhere. Old Ampere law without displacement current is inadequate for the changing capacitor. Pages5–6 correctly motivate Id=ε0 dΦE/dt and the Ampere-Maxwell law; equality with wire current presumes the full ideal plate flux and consistent signs. It is not actual conduction through the vacuum gap. Maxwell's addition and the no-monopole equation are introduced laws; the plate relation is a deduction with geometry assumptions. Page9's source language is a summary of coupled equations, not a temporally sequential causal mechanism. Page10's four integral equations and separate Lorentz force q(E+v×B) have correct signs and constants for vacuum/total sources. Closed surfaces, contour orientation and fixed-loop Faraday assumptions matter; a moving loop additionally involves motional emf.

**Pages 11–20:** All radiation/static frames were inspected, including p13's sparse black-background image. The linked animations were not executed; no time sequence is claimed from a single frame. The traveling-pulse graph on p15 shows x=vt for fixed phase of f(x−vt). Pages 16–17 deliberately use f(x+vt), propagation −x for positive v; p18 switches to sin(kx−ωt), propagation +x. This is a real convention change with explicit signs, not a contradiction. Wavelength, k=2π/λ, ω=2πf, T=1/f and v=ω/k=λf recompute correctly. In p16 “velocity v” while moving left means speed v and signed x-velocity −v. Graph amplitudes are distances from midline, not peak-to-peak values.

Recovered p19's full electromagnetic spectrum was read: each labeled wavelength/frequency pair obeys λf≈3×10⁸m/s (e.g. 3 m at 10⁸ Hz; 4×10⁻⁷ m at 7.5×10¹⁴ Hz). Band names overlap and visible color boundaries are approximate. “60 Hz ac current” is a frequency marker, not proof that a household wire is an efficient radiating antenna. Cellular labels represent the historical schematic, not current service bands. Page20's field-arrow sizes represent signed components/directions at each x; E and B at the same point are in phase. Its “out of phase oscillators” refers to different spatial positions and should not be reused to claim a phase lag between E and B. Equal drawn heights do not mean equal SI magnitudes or common units.

**Pages 21–26:** The PRS/group/in-class title slides are pointers, not full problem statements. No unidentified “Problem 1” or separate class worksheet was manufactured. Page23's c, E/B and transversality statements apply to a single traveling vacuum plane wave. They do not apply indiscriminately to standing fields, near fields or material waves; at common nodes the ratio is undefined although E=cB remains valid in magnitude. Page24's complete direction table was independently checked: x×y=z, y×z=x, z×x=y; reversing each product gives −z,−x,−y. All six listed coordinate phases p̂·r agree. Fixed polarization unit vectors are orientations of positive components; instantaneous arrows can reverse with the sinusoid.

**Pages 27–33:** The cylinder energy derivation on p28 correctly sums both field energies, sets dz=c dt, uses E=cB and ε0μ0c²=1, and obtains S=EB/μ0. The same scalar reduction requires a traveling plane wave. Page29 correctly defines S=E×B/μ0, dimensions J/(m²s)=W/m² and sinusoidal intensity I=E0B0/(2μ0)=E0²/(2μ0c)=cB0²/(2μ0). The factor 1/2 averages a squared sinusoid with peak amplitudes. Page30's steady resistive cylinder has axial E and azimuthal B, hence inward S; integrating gives I²R, as independently checked in the shared chapter review. Pages32–33 reverse circulating E while B remains upward, correctly reversing radial S. “Increasing/decreasing current” must refer to the shown positive current or magnitude: universally dUB/dt=L I I′, not merely a sign test on I′. These are ideal field illustrations, not apparatus wiring diagrams or experimental outcomes.

findings_deductions_and_limits.review:
| PDF pages | Result and audit |
|---|---|
|1–2|Choice 4: nonzero circulation due to changing gap electric flux. For the drawn disk r<b and ideal uniform plate field, ∮B·dl=μ0I r²/b² and B=μ0Ir/(2πb²). Conduction through this disk is zero. Choosing a deformed spanning surface changes the individual conduction/displacement contributions while preserving their sum.|
|3–4|Choice 1: bottom positive Q increases. In the top view B is counterclockwise, so the gap displacement current points out of the page/up in the side view, increasing the upward E. With fixed plate area Q′>0. “Real and displacement” currents here refer to different regions/surfaces, not two currents simultaneously traversing the insulating gap.|
|5–6|Choice 4: crest positions −4,0,4 give λ=4 in x-axis units and k=π/2 per x-unit. The unlabelled vertical scale is unnecessary for k. Maxima repeat correctly at all multiples of 4; avoid assigning meters when the graph gives no length unit.|
|7–8|Choice 4: −z. At a lobe with E along+y and B along+x, ŷ×x̂=−ẑ. Both arrows reverse together in the opposite lobe, so propagation is unchanged. A perspective drawing is not a physical sinusoidal particle trajectory.|
|9–10|Charge increases and S points radially inward. The prompt labels options 5–8 while the answer says 1; the correct printed prompt option is 5. This is a numbering defect, not a different physical answer. The printed equality S=E×B omits 1/μ0; it is correct only as a direction shorthand, not a magnitude or unit equation. Inward flow establishes growing Q²; the depicted Q>0 then establishes Q′>0.|
|11–12|Choice 3: the depicted positive current decreases. B points out/up, while circulating E is counterclockwise; Faraday gives dB/dt<0. Eφ×Bz points outward. Again S=E×B is missing 1/μ0 quantitatively. Decreasing stored energy establishes decreasing I²; the shown orientation fixes the positive-current interpretation.|

The shared review supplies complete technical coverage of every Chapter 13 section and all ten additional problems. Its consequential corrections include: vacuum/total-source scope of the Maxwell table; plane-wave assumptions; the printed light-speed rounding; signed versus magnitude average of standing-wave flux; missing J·E in general energy balance; capacitor/conductor outward-flux sign errors; incident versus absorbed energy in reflection momentum; peak versus mean pressure in the conducting-sheet appendix; short-dipole versus half-wave radiation model; conductor skin-depth limitation; sign/orientation and omitted premises in exercise problems. Independent computations and the exact scoped primary research are recorded there, not assumed by association.

There is no assigned lab protocol in these three files, no measured results, and no basis to infer hardware connections. Animation behavior beyond the visible frames and external worksheets remain outside actual read scope. Preparation is complete for the specified sources with these explicit technical limits; another person's teaching/readiness/closure remains unassessed.
